seo_title: Cost of Living in Manila 2026: Visa, Prices, Reviews | Relocost
seo_description: How much does it cost to live in Manila per month, do Russians need a visa, work, rent and reviews from those who relocated. A realistic moving budget in the Relocost calculator.
intro_text: The capital of the Philippines: visa-free entry for 30 days, English as a second official language, the tropics and low prices. The downsides are heavy traffic, typhoons and the air quality of a megacity.
pros: Visa-free entry for 30 days for Russian citizens
English as a second official language
A business hub with jobs and services
cons: Sharp contrasts of poverty and wealth

visa_steps.title: Visa-free entry
visa_steps.description: For Russians — visa-free up to 30 days; the stamp is issued on arrival.

visa_steps.title: Extension
visa_steps.description: The visa is easy to extend at the Bureau of Immigration, step by step, up to several months.

visa_steps.title: Renting a home
visa_steps.description: Condos are rented monthly; Makati and BGC are popular.

visa_steps.title: Connectivity and money
visa_steps.description: A local SIM card is cheap; you'll need cash in pesos and a card from a foreign bank.

visa_steps.title: Long-term stay
visa_steps.description: For settling down, the SRRV (retirement) or work visas are worth considering.

faq.question: Do Russians need a visa for Manila?
faq.answer: No, visa-free up to 30 days, with the option to extend at the local Bureau of Immigration.

faq.question: How much does it cost to live in Manila?
faq.answer: Affordable, especially food and transport. The exact budget is in the calculator above.

faq.question: Which language is spoken in Manila?
faq.answer: Tagalog, but English is a second official language and is used everywhere.

faq.question: Can I pay with a Russian card in Manila?
faq.answer: No, Russian cards don't work. You'll need cash in pesos and a card from a foreign bank.

faq.question: What is the climate like in Manila?
faq.answer: Tropical: hot year-round, with a rainy and typhoon season roughly from June to November.

faq.question: How does Manila differ from Cebu?
faq.answer: Manila is a large business megacity, while Cebu is quieter and closer to the sea and the islands.

reviews.text: Manila is convenient thanks to English and the job market; in BGC everything feels modern. The downsides are the traffic jams, the density and the typhoons — I escape to the islands to relax.
The city is full of contrasts, but lively and cheap, and language isn't a barrier. Makati is comfortable. The traffic and rainy season are the main inconveniences.
